articles.title: Trump's handpicked prosecutor resigns from DOJ probe after clash with attorney general
articles.summary: US News: A Justice Department investigation into former US officials involved in probes targeting US President Donald Trump has been hit by a new road block af.
articles.body: A Justice Department investigation into former US officials involved in probes targeting US President Donald Trump has been hit by a new road block after Joseph diGenova, the prosecutor brought in to lead the investigation, resigned following a clash with Attorney General Todd Blanche.According to a report by CNN, diGenova resigned a day after a tense phone call with Blanche. The immediate dispute centred on diGenova's attempt to prevent lawyers sent by the Justice Department headquarters from assisting his South Florida-based investigation. The disagreement came against the backdrop of other tensions surrounding how quickly the probe was progressing.The resignation is significant because the investigation is one of the Trump administration's major efforts to examine whether government officials improperly targeted the president through investigations carried out over the past decade.What is the investigation about?The probe initially focused heavily on former CIA director John Brennan, whom the Justice Department has sought to prosecute for allegedly making false statements to Congress. Brennan has been a longstanding target of Trump's criticism.But after diGenova took over the investigation in April, its scope widened considerably. His team began examining potential criminal conduct involving a broader group of Trump's political critics and former government officials connected to investigations into Trump.The inquiry, as envisioned by diGenova, stretches back to the FBI's 2016 investigation into Russian interference in the US presidential election and extends through investigations surrounding the January 6, 2021, Capitol riot and the classified-documents case involving Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence.Critics have questioned how events dating back roughly a decade could form the basis for criminal charges today, while also raising questions about the connection between some of the conduct under examination and South Florida, where a grand jury has been sitting.Why did diGenova resign?The immediate break appears to have been over control of the investigation.Justice Department headquarters had sent additional lawyers to assist the team. DiGenova sought to block them from participating, CNN reported, triggering the final confrontation with Blanche.There had also been disagreements over resources and security arrangements. DiGenova requested that a highly secure room known as a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) be built at the team's Fort Pierce office so that highly classified material could be handled there. Justice Department officials instead told the team to use an existing SCIF at an FBI office several miles away. DiGenova had also sought additional lawyers for his team, although Justice officials disputed claims that he had been denied adequate resources.The Justice Department had also been expecting criminal charges to emerge earlier this year. More recently, officials had anticipated that the first charges could come as soon as September, CNN reported.DiGenova, however, defended his slower, evidence-first approach. After his resignation, he told CNN that, as a prosecutor of more than 50 years, he made cases through “witnesses, evidence, etc.” and that such investigations take time.Despite the internal dispute, the investigation had become more active in recent weeks.CNN reported that investigators had issued a series of subpoenas seeking documents and grand jury testimony. On the day diGenova resigned, investigators were presenting a witness before a grand jury in the case.Brennan's lawyers said in a court filing that he received a subpoena requiring him to testify before a grand jury in Fort Pierce in October. They also said a prosecutor working on the case told his team that Brennan remained a target in the narrower investigation into alleged false statements.DiGenova's team has contacted former FBI and intelligence officials who had knowledge of the bureau's 2016 Russia investigation. Among those subpoenaed were former FBI lawyer Lisa Page and lawyer Dan Richman, who was a close contact of former FBI director James Comey during the period when the Russia investigation was active. A former supervisor in the FBI's Russia investigation was also interviewed for several hours after receiving immunity from prosecutors, CNN reported.The witnesses and subjects being approached show how far the inquiry has moved from its original focus on Brennan. Investigators have examined issues surrounding the intelligence community's assessment of Russian interference in the 2016 election, Brennan's leadership and even aspects of Hillary Clinton's 2016 campaign and public perceptions of Trump's relationship with Russia — subjects that have long angered Trump.What happens now?DiGenova's resignation could further delay an investigation that has already moved beyond the timeline originally expected by Justice Department officials.The department, however, does not appear to regard his departure as a setback. A US law enforcement official told CNN that Justice officials remain confident in the investigative team and expect the inquiry to regain momentum.And the investigation itself is continuing. A day after diGenova's resignation, Justice Department lawyers told Brennan's attorneys that there were multiple grand jury investigations as well as a “far-reaching” investigation in Fort Pierce examining issues connected to Mar-a-Lago and beyond, including whether Trump's civil rights had been violated, according to a court filing.The resignation, therefore, does not signal the end of Trump's effort to revisit investigations involving him.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Chiefs' new stud Kenneth Walker runs wild, Bo Nix melts down as Kansas City obliterates Broncos in MNF blowout
articles.summary: Kenneth Walker's 173-yard clinic stole the show as the Kansas City Chiefs flattened the Denver Broncos 31-10 in the AFC West's Monday Night opener.
articles.body: So much for Denver taking over the AFC West. The first Monday Night Football matchup of the 2026 season was a total disaster class for the Denver Broncos, who got flattened 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs at a rowdy Arrowhead Stadium. Everyone tuned in to see Patrick Mahomes make his return nine months after tearing his ACL and LCL last December. CHIEFS FACE CRITICAL 2026 SEASON WITH PATRICK MAHOMES RETURNING FROM ACL TEAR But while Mahomes looked crisp, Kansas City’s $43 million offseason prize stole the entire spotlight. Fresh off winning Super Bowl LX MVP honors, running back Kenneth Walker put on an absolute clinic. Walker finished with 191 total yards (173 rushing, 18 receiving) and two touchdowns ... single-handedly out gaining Davis Webb's entire Denver offense on the night. On Denver's opening drive, Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane picked off Bo Nix to hand Kansas City instant momentum, which Mahomes capitalized on with a 15-yard touchdown scramble. From there, Walker took complete control. Early in the second half, Andy Reid kept his offense on the field for a fourth-and-1 at the Kansas City 40-yard line. Walker took the handoff, hit the seam, and exploded 60 yards to the house, becoming the first Chiefs back to log over 140 rushing yards and a touchdown in a game since Kareem Hunt in 2017. Meanwhile, Denver's offense was an unmitigated trainwreck. NFL LEGEND DREW BREES REPORTEDLY ALMOST PULLED OFF A SHOCKING COMEBACK FOR BRONCOS' AFC TITLE GAME Davis Webb’s debut as Broncos offensive coordinator went down in flames as his entire unit couldn't even match the yardage output of Kansas City's lead tailback. Broncos coach Sean Payton looked like he wanted to jump out of his skin watching his new OC call plays. Outside of a quick first-quarter touchdown pass from Nix to Evan Engram that briefly tied the game at 7-7, Denver went completely ice-cold, stringing together four straight punts before halftime. The wheels completely fell off in the third quarter. Trailing 21-7, Denver got a massive break when safety Brandon Jones picked off Mahomes, handing the Broncos first-and-goal at the Kansas City 5-yard line. Instead of punching in a game-tying touchdown, Denver wet the bed. A 10-yard penalty backed the offense up, and Nix followed by dropping a snap and fumbling out of bounds near the 16-yard line to force a field goal. Nix later fumbled deep in his own territory, which Chris Jones pounced on to set up a Walker touchdown catch from Mahomes that officially put the game away. PATRICK MAHOMES SO OBSESSIVE ABOUT KNEE REHAB HE TAKES A TRAINER WITH HIM WHEN HE LEAVES TOWN Along the way, Travis Kelce provided the night's signature milestone. The All-Pro tight end ripped off an electric 59-yard catch-and-run down the sideline to officially pass Jason Witten (13,046) for second place on the NFL's all-time receiving yards list for tight ends. Kelce now trails only Hall of Famer Tony Gonzalez (15,127 yards) for the all-time spot. Old Man Kelce finished with 71 receiving yards to lead all Chiefs pass-catchers. Taylor Swift held court with Tom Cruise, subjecting cinema’s boldest stuntman / actor to a Mission: Impossible even he couldn't pull off: pretending Bo Nix is a starting quarterback. Different year, same story: the AFC West still firmly belongs to Kansas City, and Denver isn't any closer to changing that. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. articles.title: ‘Serious lapse’: Air India CEO summoned after 3 foreigners 'skip' immigration check
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Centre has summoned Air India CEO after three foreign nationals departed India without undergoing mandatory departure immigration clearance.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Centre has summoned Air India CEO after three foreign nationals departed India without undergoing mandatory departure immigration clearance, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.Sources told ANI that the ministry of civil aviation has sought an explanation from the airline after the incident, terming it a "serious security and immigration-related lapse."This comes after the civil aviation ministry issued a show-cause notice to the airline over alleged procedural lapses that allowed three Italian passengers to board a connecting flight from Delhi without completing immigration formalities earlier this month.What happenedThree Italian nationals fly into Delhi from Amritsar on September 4 and then, within an hour, depart for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight from Delhi airport without the mandatory immigration check.According to the ministry, the incident occurred during Air India's hub-and-spoke operation and involved a violation of the prescribed Standard Operating Procedure.Amritsar airport is among the airports where Air India operates flights under its ‘Hub-and-Spoke’ model.Under this arrangement, passengers complete immigration formalities at the airport of origin and can then travel to an overseas destination through a designated hub. At the hub airport, where the international flight departs, passengers are required only to undergo security checks before boarding.If a person is travelling from Amritsar via Delhi to a foreign destination, then Amritsar is the spoke and Delhi is the hub.In this case, the sources told PTI that the Italian nationals were issued boarding passes at Amritsar airport for Delhi as well as the Lufthansa flight to Munich.Meanwhile, home secretary Govind Mohan is expected to chair a meeting to discuss the incident on Tuesday. Secretary and additional secretary at the civil aviation ministry, director of Intelligence Bureau, additional secretary (UT and Foreigners) at the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration (BoI) commissioner, and Delhi airport CEO will attend the meeting, they added.The aviation ministry is also expected to make a presentation on ways to plug the gaps at the meeting.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Emmy winners 2026: ‘Widow’s Bay’ and ‘The Pitt’ dominate
articles.summary: Jean Smart earns fifth Emmy for ‘Hacks’, becoming the first to win lead comedy actress for every season of the show.
articles.body:
Emergency room drama “The Pitt” and comedy-horror “Widow’s Bay” have won television’s highest honours, the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, presented in Los Angeles.

Set in a cursed New England town, “Widow’s Bay” won the best comedy series prize on Monday, overcoming last season’s winner, “Hacks”.

Matthew Rhys, starring in “Widow’s Bay”, made history by becoming the first person to win two lead acting honours at the same ceremony. Fellow actor in the TV series, Stephen Root, won best supporting actor in a comedy, beating favourite Harrison Ford of “Shrinking”.

“Thank you, sir, for all your many years of great, great, great acting,” Root told Ford during his acceptance speech.

“Hacks” actress Jean Smart won her fifth Emmy for portraying stand-up comic Deborah Vance, making her the first actress to win the award for best lead comedy actress for every season of a show’s run. Smart has won eight Emmys overall in her acting career.

“What a ride this has been,” Smart said after receiving a standing ovation.

Actress Julia Louis-Dreyfus is the only performer to come close to Smart’s comedy lead actress sweep, having won the award for six of the seven seasons of the political satire “Veep”.

Noah Wyle, who starred as Dr “Robby” Robinavitch on “The Pitt”, told the Emmy audience it felt overwhelming to win his second straight Emmy for best lead drama actor.

“The Pitt”, set in a Pittsburgh emergency department, won its second consecutive Emmy award for best drama series, beating fellow nominees including “Pluribus”, “Paradise” and “The Diplomat”.

“This is the only club I’ve ever wanted to join. Thank you for accepting me,” Wyle said while accepting the award.

Rhea Seehorn won best actress in a drama for playing the lone character on “Pluribus”, after being nominated twice without receiving any honours for her breakthrough role on “Better Call Saul”.

Vince Gilligan, who created “Breaking Bad” and its spin-off “Better Call Saul”, won best drama writing for “Pluribus”.

“The Late Show with Stephen Colbert” won for best variety series, concluding its farewell season with six total Emmys after CBS cancelled the programme, citing financial pressures.

Colbert rejected that explanation, accusing network executives of succumbing to pressure from President Donald Trump over his frequent mockery of the administration.
